From d1a196e0a6dcddd03748468a0e9e3100790fc85c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thorsten Blum <thorsten.blum@linux.dev>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 12:30:51 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] platform/x86: dell-wmi-sysman: Don't hex dump plaintext
 password data
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

set_new_password() hex dumps the entire buffer, which contains plaintext
password data, including current and new passwords. Remove the hex dump
to avoid leaking credentials.

Fixes: e8a60aa7404b ("platform/x86: Introduce support for Systems Management Driver over WMI for Dell Systems")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Thorsten Blum <thorsten.blum@linux.dev>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260303113050.58127-2-thorsten.blum@linux.dev
Reviewed-by: Ilpo Järvinen <ilpo.jarvinen@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Ilpo Järvinen <ilpo.jarvinen@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/platform/x86/dell/dell-wmi-sysman/passwordattr-interface.c b/drivers/platform/x86/dell/dell-wmi-sysman/passwordattr-interface.c
index 86ec962aace9..e586f7957946 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/x86/dell/dell-wmi-sysman/passwordattr-interface.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/x86/dell/dell-wmi-sysman/passwordattr-interface.c
@@ -93,7 +93,6 @@ int set_new_password(const char *password_type, const char *new)
 	if (ret < 0)
 		goto out;
 
-	print_hex_dump_bytes("set new password data: ", DUMP_PREFIX_NONE, buffer, buffer_size);
 	ret = call_password_interface(wmi_priv.password_attr_wdev, buffer, buffer_size);
 	/* on success copy the new password to current password */
 	if (!ret)
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Files Modified

**`drivers/platform/x86/dell/dell-wmi-sysman/passwordattr-interface.c`**
- Removed a call to `print_hex_dump_bytes()` that dumped the entire password buffer (containing plaintext current and new passwords) to the kernel log.

### Relationships Between Modifications

This is a single-file, single-line change with no cross-file dependencies. The modification directly fixes a security vulnerability (credential leakage) by eliminating the debug output that exposed plaintext password data during the `set_new_password()` function execution.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
print_hex_dump_bytes("set new password data: ", DUMP_PREFIX_NONE, buffer, buffer_size);
```
Reason: This line outputs the entire buffer, which contains plaintext current and new passwords, to the kernel log, thereby leaking sensitive credential data.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
	ret = call_password_interface(wmi_priv.password_attr_wdev, buffer, buffer_size);
```
Reason: The `print_hex_dump_bytes` line is removed, so the password data is no longer dumped. The code now directly proceeds to call the password interface without exposing the buffer contents.
